Parsnips — Architecture & Schema

Sitting → Section → Speaker → Content. Deterministic where possible, model only where judgement is needed.
Requirements: REQUIREMENTS.md · Design decisions D-1 … D-10

01Pipeline architecture

Five stages. Three of them involve no model at all — the mechanical work is deterministic and reproducible. The model appears once, in Stage 2, and it returns sentence ids rather than quotations: the assembler substitutes the stored text afterwards. That is what makes every published quote verbatim by construction (R-2.1, R-2.2).

02Entity relationships

One chain gives provenance: sitting → report → turn → sentence. Everything derived hangs off it and refers back by id. There is no entity called "brief" with its own copy of the text — a claim points at the sentences it rests on.

Why there is no “brief” entity holding its own text. If a brief stored a copy of the words, the copy could drift from the record and no check would catch it — that is precisely how a reworded quotation would enter the system. Instead a claim stores only an assertion plus the ids of the sentences it rests on; the quotation is substituted from sentence.text at assembly time. A model that mangles a quote in its head has no way to publish the mangled version.

03Schema

Legend: PK primary key · FK foreign key · NN not null. Row counts are measured, not estimates.

sitting 331 rows · one calendar day Parliament sat
columntypenotes
id PKdateISO date — the natural key
parliament_no NNint13, 14 or 15 across the archive
volume_nointHansard volume
sitting_nointsitting number within the volume
collected / max_resultintreports fetched vs the API's own claim
coverage_ratiofloatdeclared enumeration coverage (R-1.3)
source_hashstring(16)content fingerprint — detects a re-fetch that differs
report 20,962 rows · one Hansard API record
columntypenotes
id PKstringe.g. bill-366 — the API's stable identity
sitting_id FK NNdate→ sitting.id
type NNenumbill · statement · motion · budget · adjournment · oral · written · correction · tribute
titletextas printed in Hansard — never used as a key
report_version NNstringformat era (sprs3) — recorded, never inferred (R-6.3)
words / turns_countintdenormalised counts for reporting
turn 94,272 rows · one speaker's contiguous contribution
columntypenotes
id PKstring<report_id>:t<order_index>
report_id FK NNstring→ report.id
speaker_label_id FKint→ speaker_label.id; nullable when unattributed (D-4)
order_index NNintposition in the record — the debate's own order
attributed NNbooltrue = label from the record; false = carried forward (4.0% of turns)
words NNintmedian 67, p90 506, max 16,209
is_proceduralboolchair business — retained, filterable at display
sentence 754,082 rows · the unit of citation
columntypenotes
sid PKstringstable id within a turn, e.g. s00012
turn_id FK NNstring→ turn.id
text NNtextthe sentence, verbatim from the record
order_in_turn NNintpreserves reading order
char_start / char_end NNintoffsets into the normalised report text — proves position
sha256 NNstringproves content — re-slice and compare
excludedboolexcluded from prompts (procedural / courtesy / too short)
exclude_reasonenumnever silent — an unrecorded drop is indistinguishable from a bug (R-2.5)
speaker_label 1,330 rows · the label exactly as recorded
columntypenotes
id PKint
label NNtexte.g. The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
is_chair NNboolMr Speaker / Chairman — section furniture, not a person
person_idintNULL for now, deliberately. Reserved for a later identity layer (R-6.9)
turn_summary derived · one summary per turn, or per sub-split
columntypenotes
id PKstring
turn_id FK NNstring→ turn.id
sub_index NNint0 for a whole turn; 0..N when a >1,500-word turn is split (D-9)
text NNtext~25–35 words — the 10-second reading budget (R-3.7)
modelstringwhich model produced it
prompt_hashstringreproducibility: same input → same prompt
claim derived · the citation-carrying unit
columntypenotes
id PKstring
summary_id FK NNstring→ turn_summary.id
text NNtextthe assertion, in plain language
cites NNstring[]sentence sids. The only source of the quotation
quote NNtextsubstituted from sentence.text at assembly — never model-written
attribution_source NNenumrecord | inferred — rendered differently on the page (D-4)
verifiedboolset by Stage 4; false means the claim is not published
gate_result derived · every gate decision, recorded
columntypenotes
id PKint
target_type / target_id NNstringwhat was checked (item, claim, report, sitting)
gate_name NNenumprovenance · coverage · attribution · completeness
passed NNboolfalse ⇒ withhold, never publish (D-1, D-3)
detailtextwhy it failed — the only artefact a human reviews (D-2)
checked_at NNtimestamp

Stage 1 · what exists today

  • • 3,912 policy items built
  • • 754,082 sentences with stable sids
  • • 8,415 chunks, defined as id lists
  • • invariants verified corpus-wide
  • • not yet: char offsets, sha256, exclusion reasons

Stage 2 · the only model stage

  • • returns sentence ids, not quotations
  • • ~10s reading budget per summary
  • • small items: one call whole
  • • heavy items: map → reduce
  • • model choice still open

Gates · four, all failing closed

  • • provenance: sid resolves + hash matches
  • • coverage: nothing silently dropped
  • • attribution: recorded vs inferred
  • • completeness: whole item summarised
  • • each needs a test that breaks it (R-2.9)

The provenance chain

  • • claim → cites[] → sentence.sid
  • • sid → char_start/char_end
  • • re-slice source → compare sha256
  • • a quote is proven, not trusted
  • • re-verifiable after publication

Parsnips · architecture & schema v0.1 · 17 Sep 2026
Requirements phase — no implementation started. Row counts measured via tools/metrics.py.
